- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- In periods of high volatility or sentiment divergence, model tends to ignore short-term mean reversion; enforce 3–5 day moving average alignment with true price.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish/bearish cycles, model often fails to capture cycle timing; align forecast with sentiment swing points rather than linear extrapolation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; cap initial forecast values at 1–2% below recent 7-day average to avoid premature peak.
- When sentiment is consistently high but price declines, model fails to anticipate reversal; add a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment >0.7 and price drops >1% from recent peak.
